segments.he: עַל יְדֵי אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים וְשִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ עִקַּר
segments.en: However, there is a great and powerful obstacle — the obstacle of livelihood: for every person is deeply occupied with his livelihood, and therefore does not engage fully even in this easy counsel, to return to G-d through the holy speech of the twenty-two letters of the aleph-beis. But in truth, even this is no obstacle at all. For one must remind oneself of the truth — that it is impossible in any way to draw one's livelihood to oneself through one's own toil and effort alone. For it would be heresy, Heaven forfend, to say "My strength and the power of my hand have made me this wealth" [Devarim 8:17] — Heaven forfend, G-d spare us. Rather, one must believe in G-d, that all livelihood comes from Him alone. As it is written: "And you shall remember Hashem your G-d, for He is the One who gives you the power to make wealth" [Devarim 8:18], and as it is written in this Psalm: "The eyes of all look to You with hope, and You give them their food in its time; You open... and satisfy" [Tehillim 145:15-16]. And this is the greatness of this Psalm — that it contains two things together: the aleph-beis as the totality of holy speech, and the mention of livelihood as coming from Him. Therefore one who goes in this path is certainly assured that he is a son of the World to Come. For through this is the essential teshuvah and drawing-close to Him from wherever one may be — even if one has not merited to toil and labor in His service like the Tzaddikim and the righteous and the pious who came before us. And even so, if one will not let oneself fall forever, and strengthens oneself to speak words in any case always before G-d — with many cries and supplications and requests — certainly ultimately one will return to G-d. But livelihood must not prevent him from this — rather he should trust in G-d that He will provide for him with compassion.

segments.he: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי נְגִינָה שֶׁבָּהֶם נֶאֱמַר סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים.
segments.en: And even if one is a businessman or craftsman — even so, one should know the truth that strength alone does not make a man mighty. And whatever one does, one cannot receive one's livelihood through one's toil and effort alone, except through G-d's salvation and kindness — as each person knows from experience, that the essential livelihood comes when G-d arranges some profit for him. And especially worries and anxieties do not help at all — on the contrary, they greatly damage livelihood. Therefore even the businessman and craftsman can find for himself several hours a day to engage in saying Tehillim and hisbodidus — to sanctify the speech of the aleph-beis — and through this he will certainly return to G-d.

segments.he: כִּי אִיתָא בְּדִבְרֵי אֲדוֹנֵנוּ מוֹרֵנוּ וְרַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בְּסִימָן רל"ז שֶׁעִקַּר הַהִתְחַבְּרוּת עַל יְדֵי נְגִינָה בִּבְחִינַת (בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ט) הַפַּעַם יִלָּוֶה אִישִׁי אֵלַי הַנֶּאֱמַר כְּשֶׁנּוֹלַד לֵוִי שֶׁעוֹסְקִין בְּשִׁיר עַל הַדּוּכָן וְכוּ' עַיֵּן שָׁם. הַיְנוּ כִּי שִׁיר וְנִגּוּן בְּחִינַת תְּהִלִּים עַל יְדֵי זֶה עִקַּר הַהִתְחַבְּרוּת שֶׁל כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם דּוֹדָהּ כִּי עִקַּר הָרִחוּק חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הוּא מֵחֲמַת הַוִּכּוּחַ הַנַּ"ל.
segments.en: The summary of all these matters: the essential distance from teshuvah comes from the fact that we need to awaken ourselves to return to Him, and such awakening as is fitting is very difficult. Especially for one who has already distanced himself and done what he has done. Yet even so, all desire to fear His Name — but it is hard and heavy for them to awaken, and all want G-d to awaken them and return them to good. But when they know and believe in the truth — that G-d chooses precisely this: that our will and desire be always to draw close to Him; and that we need nothing but to "take words" and return to Him — as it is written: "Take with you words and return to Hashem" [Hoshea 14:3], and our Sages taught: "I ask of you nothing but words." And in truth even the words themselves come from Him — we only need to strive to take them with us and to speak them before Him. And this is "Take with you" — take precisely — the words are already prepared by Him, and G-d asks that we take them with us to return to Him. And He teaches and instructs us how to say before Him, as it is written: "Say to Him: 'Forgive all iniquity...'" [Hoshea 14:3]. And whoever truly knows all this — will certainly return to G-d easily from wherever he is, even if things happen to befall him. For he can always take words from G-d, if he desires — until ultimately he will return to Him and He will have mercy upon him. And this is the aspect of the greatness of the value of saying Tehillim that Rabbainu revealed — that through this certainly one merits teshuvah. And through this the complete redemption will come speedily in our days — as long as one engages in saying Tehillim with intention, listening with one's ear and heart to what one says — certainly one will return to G-d. For truly everything is from Him, and G-d desires only the will and the awakening and the effort after truth — for without any awakening at all, it is impossible. But in truth, everything is from Him.

segments.he: שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל רוֹצִים שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ יְעוֹרְרֵם תְּחִלָּה וִישִׁיבֵם אֵלָיו.
segments.en: It is explained in Rabbainu's words, of blessed memory, that one can merit through abundant hisbodidus and longing for G-d — through which one draws souls — and through this one merits that all one's food is in the aspect of the lechem hapanim [the Showbread, the Bread of Faces]. As explained in the Torah "Ais Lan Beiri B'Davra" [Likutay Moharan I:31].

segments.he: וְהוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה שֶׁכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל תִּתְעוֹרֵר תְּחִלָּה. אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הָעֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי נְגִינָה מֵעֵלָּא לְתַתָּא וּמִתַּתָּא לְעֵלָּא בִּבְחִינַת מִזְמוֹר לְדָוִד לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר.
segments.en: This matter of the greatness of melitzah [eloquence, fine speech] is very necessary for every person who desires true and eternal life. For one who wishes to approach the holy, to walk in the ways of G-d, to return to Him — the general counsel, which is the foundation of all counsels, is hisbodidus and intimate conversation between one and one's Creator, as we have explained on many occasions. That is, to train oneself every day to go to a designated place to seclude oneself there and to pour out one's speech before Him, as a man speaks to his friend — and to multiply arguments and importings and requests and persuasions in the language one speaks (in our lands, in the Ashkenazic language [Yiddish] that we speak) — that G-d help him and merit him to return from his evil deeds and to draw close to Him.

segments.he: וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים אוֹמֵר שִׁירָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שׁוֹרָה עָלָיו רוּחַ הַקּדֶשׁ וְלִפְעָמִים לְהֵפֶךְ שֶׁשּׁוֹרָה עָלָיו רוּחַ הַקּדֶשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹמֵר שִׁירָה הַיְנוּ כַּנַּ"ל שֶׁמִּזְמוֹרֵי תְּהִלִּים כָּלוּל מִשְּׁנֵי הַבְּחִינוֹת מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא קדֶם וּמֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵלָּא קדֶם כַּנַּ"ל. עַל כֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְּהִלִּים עִקַּר הַהִתְחַבְּרוּת וְהַהִתְקָרְבוּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם. מֵאַחַר שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְלָלִין יַחַד שְׁנֵי הַהִתְעוֹרְרוּת. כִּי תְּהִלִּים מְעוֹרֵר לֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהִשְׁתּוֹקֵק לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְזֶה נֶחְשָׁב לְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁלָּנוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הַכּל מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכַנַּ"ל. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת תָּכִין לִבָּם תַּקְשִׁיב אָזְנֶיךָ. שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ מֵכִין לְבָבֵנוּ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֵלָיו.
segments.en: And for this matter, the issue of melitzah is a great thing — that one should train oneself to expand one's conversation and to multiply arguments, and to seek to find for oneself each time new words of supplication and persuasion and fitting arguments and many words of awakening of compassion — in the manner of those who importune, in the manner of those who come before kings and judges to plead for their lives, when they know within themselves that they are guilty, and they come to appease them. Then from the great bitterness of their soul, words of supplication and persuasion without end flow from their hearts naturally — until sometimes they move the heart of the king or judge to the point that he begins to weep along with them as well, out of great compassion — and the like of such speech, greatly. For regarding intimate conversation between oneself and one's Creator, which is the essential true purpose, that one must merit thereby to eternal life forever and ever, and to be saved from the pit and from the mire — for this purpose one needs all kinds of speech in the world: supplications and requests and appeasements and persuasions and importings and compassion and pleas and arguments — and the like of all this greatly. And all these kinds of speech are all encompassed within the aspect of melitzah. For all this is drawn in its root from the supernal melitzah, from which King Dovid, peace be upon him, founded the book of Tehillim through his holy spirit — for through his holy spirit he merited to holy melitzah in truth.

segments.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוּא מַקְשִׁיב אָזְנָיו לִשְׁמעַ דִּבּוּרֵינוּ כְּאִלּוּ הֵם יוֹצְאִים מֵאִתָּנוּ בְּעַצְמֵנוּ. רַק שֶׁאָנוּ מְחֻיָּבִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְהִתְעוֹרֵר לָזֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ לְהִשְׁתּוֹקֵק וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל זֶה שֶׁיָּכִין לְבָבֵנוּ אֵלָיו. שֶׁזֶּהוּ בְּעַצְמוֹ בְּחִינַת הַתְּפִלָּה תָּכִין לִבָּם תַּקְשִׁיב אָזְנֶיךָ. וְכֵן מִתְפַּלֵּל דָּוִד בְּסֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים הַרְבֵּה עַל זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים נ"א) אֲדנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וְכוּ'. כִּי תְּהִלִּים הוּא בְּחִינַת הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְשִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לְהַרְבּוֹת בָּזֶה מְאד. כִּי עַל יְדֵי אֲמִירַת תְּהִלִּים וְשִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִין לְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ עַל הַכּל וּלְבַקֵּשׁ לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל זֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁנּוּכַל לְבַקְּשׁוֹ הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ ה' אֵלֶיךָ וְכוּ' בֶּאֱמֶת. נִמְצָא שֶׁהַכּל מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן נֶחְשָׁב לְהִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁלָּנוּ מֵאַחַר שֶׁאָנוּ מִתְעוֹרְרִים עַל כָּל פָּנִים לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל זֶה וְכַנַּ"ל וְהָבֵן הֵיטֵב. כִּי בְּוַדַּאי בְּלִי שׁוּם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת כְּלָל אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְקָרֵב. (שָׁם אוֹת יא):
segments.en: Until he merited that his holy book, the book of Tehillim, encompasses all the languages of holy melitzah — and therefore in truth it has great power to awaken a person's heart and to awaken supernal compassion, when it is said with heartfelt intention, and to bring a person close to G-d. And the essential greatness of melitzah is for the sake of the true purpose — to merit through it to draw close to G-d. And whoever merits such melitzah, and spends his days giving eloquent speech before G-d in prayer and supplication — or to give eloquent speech to Israel to awaken them to His service in truth — certainly, praiseworthy is he and praiseworthy is his portion. And one who does not merit this fully — this is not a hindrance to his service. For G-d does not deal harshly with His creatures. And He does not want from a person to do what is beyond his capacity. And one can draw close to G-d through one's conversation however it is — and however one speaks will be considered before G-d as beautiful and fitting melitzah. For what is essential before G-d is truth — that the intention of one's heart be in truth. For "Hashem is close to all who call Him — to all who call Him in truth" [Tehillim 145:18]. And whoever has sincere intention — then even if he has never been eloquent and has never learned the ways of fine speech — even so, his mouth and heart open of themselves, and he can speak beautiful words and fitting arguments before G-d, which are drawn from the aspect of holy melitzah.
